item.title: Austin weather: Video captures car spinning down icy road
item.description: Officials urged drivers to stay off the roads in Austin when the Arctic blast hit and one person's video shows exactly why.

item.title: Austin activates cold weather shelters due to overnight freezing temperatures
item.description: The City of Austin has activated its cold weather shelters for the rest of the week.The overnight shelters will be open from Wednesday, Jan. 28, until Sunday, Feb. 1. It will operate overnight only and will not be open 24 hours a day.According to the city, those who need shelter will need to go to One Texas Center, at 505 Barton Springs Road, from 6 to 8 p.m. to register each night.CapMetro bus routes to the OTC are lines: 1, 7, 10, 20, 30, 105, 801. item.title: Austin police rescue kittens found abandoned in freezing weather
item.description: Eight kittens, who were found abandoned in a cage in freezing weather, were rescued by the Austin Police Department.Austin police said on Tuesday, Jan. 27, a 911 call reported kittens being found in a cage on Great Northern Blvd.When an officer arrived, eight kittens were found freezing in a cage along a sidewalk with no shelter, food, or water. item.title: Crews respond to broken water pipes as temperatures begin to warm up
item.description: As the ice continues to thaw in Central Texas, crews are responding to burst pipes. But this time, it’s a very different story than what we saw during the big freeze five years ago.Since Saturday, the Austin Fire Department reported responding to more than 90 calls for broken pipes. item.title: Texas State University PD swears in new therapy dogs
item.description: Texas State University has two new "paw-fficers." They're therapy dogs who were sworn in as part of the university police force. item.title: Barton Springs-Edwards Aquifer warns groundwater levels are nearing historic lows
item.description: After nearly four years of drought, the aquifer that feeds Barton Springs and supplies drinking water to thousands, is nearing historic lows.Officials say if current conditions continue, a Stage 4 emergency response could be declared for the first time in the district's 39-year history.The Barton Springs-Edwards Aquifer Conservation District is warning groundwater levels within the district are approaching historic lows."We're almost missing an entire year's worth of rainfall," said Shay Hlavaty

item.title: Alex Pretti: Austin nurses gather at vigil to honor man killed by ICE
item.description: National Nurses United, the country’s largest union of registered nurses, has mobilized a week of action, hosting vigils to seek justice for a nurse killed by immigration officers in Minnesota. One took place at Ascension Seton Medical Center in Central Austin on Wednesday evening.Nurses and community members gathered in honor of fellow health care worker Alex Pretti. item.title: Texas Democrats demand 5-year-old's release from ICE facility in Dilley
item.description: Hundreds packed into Progreso Hall in west San Antonio Wednesday night, as calls for the disbandment of ICE rang through the community rally.Representative Greg Casar could be heard chanting, "Free Liam Ramos, free our children," in reference to five-year-old Liam Conejo Ramos, who was taken into ICE custody alongside his father in Minnesota last week.
